C-EDIT-NATIVE-ROUTING.IntentSummary: Stop overriding OpenCode's built-in edit tooling. Remove the plugin's replace profile (the plugin-owned `edit` tool that shadows the host built-in by id), stop registering any tool named `edit`, and let the host's built-in `edit` and `apply_patch` serve their native cohorts. The plugin keeps only `hashline_edit` and `str_replace_editor`. The routing vocabulary becomes native tool names `apply_patch | edit | str_replace_editor | hashline_edit` (`replace` and `passthrough` are removed and rejected loudly), the default table routes deepseek→str_replace_editor, kimi/qwen/glm→edit, gpt/codex→apply_patch, default→hashline_edit, and chat.message leaves exactly one edit tool visible per session (hiding the built-in edit for deepseek/hashline cohorts, never touching apply_patch).

T-001.Title: Routing vocabulary: replace/passthrough removed, native tool names apply_patch/edit/str_replace_editor/hashline_edit

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: routing.ts EDIT_MODES equals ["apply_patch", "edit", "str_replace_editor", "hashline_edit"]; parseEditMode rejects "replace" and "passthrough" with a message listing the four accepted values; resolveEditMode keeps provider-then-model first-match semantics.

plugin-toggle-config.ts DEFAULT_HASHLINE_EDIT_ROUTING becomes { default: "hashline_edit", rules: { deepseek: "str_replace_editor", kimi: "edit", qwen: "edit", glm: "edit", gpt: "apply_patch", codex: "apply_patch" } } and defaultHashlineRoutingCopy keeps producing a deep copy of it.
schemas/vvoc/v3.json routing default and rules enums become ["apply_patch", "edit", "str_replace_editor", "hashline_edit"].

routing.test.ts asserts the four-value vocabulary, the new default table, loud rejection of replace/passthrough (including rules values and default), and unchanged provider-before-model / first-match / case-insensitivity / fallback-to-default behavior.
vvoc-config.test.ts routing expectations update to the four-value enum (the "patch" rejection test keeps failing loudly on an unknown mode).

T-002.Title: Remove the replace profile: delete replace-engine.ts and stop registering the edit tool

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src/plugins/hashline-edit/replace-engine.ts and src/plugins/hashline-edit.replace-engine.test.ts are deleted; nothing imports applyReplaceEdit/formatReplaceSuccess/ReplaceEditParams anymore.

index.ts EDIT_TYPE_TOOLS becomes ["hashline_edit", "str_replace_editor"]; the tool map registers only hashline_edit and str_replace_editor; executeReplaceEdit and ReplaceEditArgs are removed; the REPLACE_EDIT_DESCRIPTION export and its tool-description.ts section are removed.
index.ts module contract, module map, and change summary reflect the two-tool registration and the removed replace profile.

hashline-edit.test.ts registration test asserts plugin.tool has exactly hashline_edit and str_replace_editor and no edit key; the "replace edit enforces prior read and applies exact matches" test is replaced by a host-edit visibility test (below in T-003) or removed together with the profile.

T-003.Title: Per-model visibility with the built-in edit: chat.message leaves exactly one edit tool visible

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: visibleToolsForMode returns: hashline_edit → ["hashline_edit"], edit → ["edit"], str_replace_editor → ["str_replace_editor"], apply_patch → [] (the host gate owns apply_patch); the mode-to-visible mapping is exercised in routing/visibility tests.

chat.message sets tools[name]=false for every edit tool in ["hashline_edit","edit","str_replace_editor"] not in the mode's visible set, and never sets tools[apply_patch]; the built-in edit remains visible for mode `edit` (no tools[edit]=false) and is hidden for str_replace_editor/hashline_edit modes.

hashline-edit.test.ts visibility expectations update: deepseek → { hashline_edit:false, edit:false } (unchanged), qwen/glm → { hashline_edit:false, str_replace_editor:false } (unchanged), minimax → { edit:false, str_replace_editor:false } (unchanged), gpt → { hashline_edit:false, edit:false, str_replace_editor:false } (unchanged); the routing-config override test and any apply_patch assertions stay consistent with the new vocabulary.
tool.execute.before rejects only plugin-tool calls (hashline_edit/str_replace_editor) for sessions whose routed mode targets a different tool, and never blocks tool "edit" or "apply_patch".

T-004.Title: Docs and durable state: README routing section, graph, and verification updated

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: README per-model editing bullets and the HashlineEditPlugin/routing sections describe the four native modes (apply_patch | edit | str_replace_editor | hashline_edit), the default table (deepseek→str_replace_editor, kimi/qwen/glm→edit, gpt/codex→apply_patch, default→hashline_edit), and that the built-in host edit serves the edit cohort; replace/passthrough wording is removed.

.grace/graph/main.xml M-PLUGIN-HASHLINE-EDIT purpose/paths reflect two registered tools (hashline_edit, str_replace_editor), the native routing vocabulary, and host-owned edit/apply_patch; no module ownership or dependency claims go stale.
.grace/verification/main.xml V-M-PLUGIN-HASHLINE-EDIT test-file list drops replace-engine.test.ts and the scenario/expected text describe the four-value routing and host-edit cohort.
opencode.test.ts expectedPlugins materialization assertions still pass with the new default routing table (materializeHashlineEditEntry true-path includes the new table).

T-005.Title: Smoke verification: host built-in edit serves the edit cohort end to end

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: On a scratch project with the plugin enabled and routing default table, a qwen/glm-routed session exposes only the built-in edit (hashline_edit/str_replace_editor hidden), read output carries no hash anchors, and an oldString/newString edit applies through the host with camelCase args and no line duplication.
A deepseek-routed session exposes only str_replace_editor; a gpt/codex-routed session exposes only the host apply_patch; an unmatched model exposes only hashline_edit with anchored read output.
Smoke findings (tools visible per cohort, edit applied, no duplication, no anchor leakage into the edit cohort) are recorded as evidence in the execution summary.

Verification.Command: manual smoke session on a scratch project with the built plugin
